analysis:
Both units are base-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 2176-2634). The only changed head content in this file is a v0.10.10 candidate release-notes section at the top (head lines 11-39), where waitlist gating is added for new sandbox setups and new cluster pairs. The patch excerpt is truncated, and only the base-text units were supplied, so the new head text is not visible to cite.

The changelog is documentation, not executable code. I found no change to the trust boundaries, keys, attestation, encryption or authorization controls in the supplied evidence. The base text I examined describes already-shipped behavior: add-on hold hardening (TB-012, T-059, T-060), SSD prefix-cache checkpoints (T-041), and sandbox and GPU-limit setup (TB-013, TB-014). I did not re-verify any of those, and a changelog is not proof of code behavior.

Open questions for integration, none of them a finding:
1. The v0.10.10 notes describe a coordinator-side waitlist approval gate for `darkbloom sandbox setup` and `darkbloom cluster`. The implementation is not in this batch. A later pass should check that the gate fails closed and cannot be bypassed, and that it does not interfere with T-061 (installer integrity) or T-062 (the non-interactive GPU-limit command).
2. The notes say existing setups are never re-asked. That claim cannot be verified from this batch.
3. The notes say that when the coordinator does not offer waitlists, setups go on as before. That fail-open default is stated in the patch excerpt but is not enforceable from this batch. If the gate was meant as a security control, the fail-open behavior would matter, but the notes present it as an availability and rollout feature.

No security regressions were identified in the supplied text.
